title: How to Find and Fix the Causes of Your Bad Habits
coreMove: Name the real relief a bad habit is buying before choosing a better response.
sourcePressure: Bad habits often persist because they appear to solve a problem or relieve a feeling, and better change starts by naming that underlying cause accurately.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Calling the bad habit irrational before identifying the problem it seems to solve.

hook: starting with a definition of bad habit
counterintuition: the problem is not motivation alone

exampleSpecs.domain: a newsroom copy editor diagnosing why she raids the vending machine after corrections
exampleSpecs.audience: an editor ashamed of late-night sugar runs
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the snack is named as relief from humiliation rather than hunger
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she writes the exact feeling after the redline call and chooses a different decompression before leaving the desk
exampleSpecs.firstImage: red correction marks glowing on a newsroom monitor

exampleSpecs.domain: a public defender identifying why she checks messages during client interviews
exampleSpecs.audience: a lawyer whose attention keeps breaking
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the phone habit solves anxiety about missed court updates
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she places the docket alert on a clerk channel and names the craving as certainty, not distraction
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a docket sheet clipped under a phone face down

exampleSpecs.domain: a boat mechanic replacing angry tool tossing with a fault tag
exampleSpecs.audience: a mechanic whose outburst slows repairs
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the bad habit is seen as a flawed answer to confusion
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: when the bolt strips, he ties a red fault tag to the part instead of throwing the wrench
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a stripped bolt under a dangling red tag

exampleSpecs.domain: a hospice volunteer noticing why she jokes after difficult visits
exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer worried her humor is disrespectful
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the habit is understood as relief from helplessness
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: her supervisor asks what problem the joke solves, and she names the silence she is trying to escape
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a volunteer badge lying on a quiet nurses station counter

exampleSpecs.domain: a seed-company salesperson reframing discount overpromising
exampleSpecs.audience: a rep who keeps promising deals finance rejects
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the bad habit solves fear of disappointing growers
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he traces each overpromise to the moment a grower goes quiet and scripts an honest pause instead
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a seed order form with a circled discount field

exampleSpecs.domain: a college resident assistant diagnosing why she avoids conflict rounds
exampleSpecs.audience: an RA whose floor rules keep slipping
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether avoidance is named as buying temporary peace
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she marks the feeling before skipping a knock and replaces the escape with a prepared first sentence
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a dorm hallway quiet under blue exit signs

skillTargets: infer the real problem a bad habit seems to solve
choose replacement responses matched to the underlying need

tryThisNowSpec: When a bad habit urge appears, write the problem it is trying to solve in seven words or fewer before choosing your response.
